name: Sewers
summary: Beneath the hills west of Lordaeron's ruined palace, the Sewers offer a second way into the Undercity. Their stone passage carries bat handlers and travelers past the elevators descending from the throne room.

sections.title: A Backdoor into the Catacombs
sections.body: The Sewers once drained Lordaeron's royal capital. Now Sylvanas Windrunner's Forsaken fold those old stone channels into the Undercity's defenses. The passage opens west of the surface ruins, near a Scarlet Watchtower in Tirisfal Glades, then slopes directly inside. Forsaken bat handlers fly riders through the cavernous conduit into the Undercity's subterranean rings, avoiding the slow cage lifts. The route also skirts the fortified courtyards, leaving a dangerous weakness that hostile infiltrators seek to exploit.

faq.q: Where does the sewer tunnel lead outside?
faq.answer: The sewer passage opens in the hills of Tirisfal Glades, west of the main gates to the Ruins of Lordaeron. The Scarlet Watchtower overlooking the lake is nearby.

faq.q: Why would anyone use the sewers instead of the main entrance?
faq.answer: The main entrance descends from the palace ruins by iron cage elevators, which can be slow and dangerous during an attack. The Sewers provide a direct, sloped route for Forsaken bat traffic and a quick way out without waiting for the lifts.

faq.q: Is the sewer safe from Alliance raiders?
faq.answer: No. The Sewers bypass Lordaeron's fortified gatehouse and throne room, making them a breach point for Alliance scouts and strike teams trying to enter the Forsaken capital unseen.

angles.text: For the Forsaken, the Sewers are an essential lifeline and flight corridor, keeping the Undercity connected to the rest of Lordaeron without crowding the courtyard elevators.
If you assault the Forsaken capital, the Sewers offer a covert route past the heavily defended surface ruins.
